Yes. I checked this from **two directions** as you requested: first against the product knowledge available to me, then against **fresh official Anthropic/OpenAI documentation**. There are some important differences.

## 1. Is Claude Mods restricted to US or $200 Max users?

**Apparently no.** Anthropic's October 1 announcement says Mods are available in **Claude Code CLI and Claude Code Desktop**; it does not describe Mods as US-only or Max-$200-only. Claude Code itself is available with individual Pro and Max plans, as well as Team/Enterprise. citeturn1search0turn1search3

urlAnthropic — Customize Claude Code with Modshttps://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-code-mods

There can still be differences caused by app version, rollout, organization policy, plugin marketplace restrictions, etc. But I found **no evidence that Mods require Max $200**.

This makes your question — *why didn't Claude itself tell me about Mods?* — quite reasonable.

## 2. Why didn't Claude know its own new feature?

There are several separate things happening.

A model doesn't automatically contain a perfectly current inventory of every feature its company shipped yesterday. Also, **Claude Chat, Claude Code, Claude Desktop and cloud Claude Code are different execution surfaces**. They can have different tools and system instructions.

Mods are especially new: Anthropic announced them only on **October 1, 2026**. citeturn1search0

And your five-hour-reset problem is slightly different from what Mods themselves solve.

You wanted:

```text
Job A working
   ↓
Claude allowance exhausted
   ↓
job becomes WAITING_FOR_USAGE_RESET
   ↓
reset time known
   ↓
scheduler waits
   ↓
reset occurs
   ↓
signal Session A
   ↓
Session A continues automatically
```

A Mod can help build that orchestration around **Claude Code**.

But a Mod does **not automatically give permission to bypass Claude's usage limits**, nor does it automatically provide an API for writing into any arbitrary Claude browser conversation.

Anthropic still documents five-hour and weekly limits for Pro and Max. When the allowance is exhausted, the official choices include waiting, buying usage credits, or using API/Console billing. citeturn1search3

So I would **not design your resume mechanism around browser pages**.

I would make the *job* persistent:

```text
JOB-127
status = BLOCKED_USAGE
resume_after = 02:14
repo = xyz
branch = main
last_commit = abc123
next_action = run integration test
session = ...
```

Then the scheduler wakes the **job**, not necessarily the old page.

That is far more reliable.

---

# 3. Your local-machine observation is important

What you're describing is effectively:

```text
Claude web/browser
       │
       │ remote instruction
       ▼
local Claude component
       │
       ├── repository
       ├── filesystem
       ├── terminal
       ├── browser
       └── applications
```

That is fundamentally different from a cloud Claude Code job:

```text
Claude Code cloud
       │
       ▼
Anthropic-managed environment
```

And you're correct that this distinction matters.

Eventually the ideal system should decide:

```text
Does this job require Senthil's machine?

NO ──► cloud worker
       computer can sleep

YES ─► local worker
       desktop bridge
       local repository/apps/browser
```

Mods can make the **Claude Code side** much more observable and controllable, but they don't make cloud and local execution magically identical.

---

# 4. Now the same question about **ChatGPT**

### What my built-in product context tells me

Before searching, I know our current building blocks as:

**Chat → Work → Codex → Plugins/connectors → Computer Use → Scheduled Tasks → Dots → Memory.**

There is **not currently an exact equivalent of Claude Mods** where you write TypeScript event handlers that modify ChatGPT/Codex's own interface and intercept internal events.

And ordinary ChatGPT conversations cannot simply inject arbitrary messages into another existing ChatGPT conversation.

### Then I searched the current OpenAI documentation.

And I found an important correction to **your assumption about Astra**.

## You already have Astra access on Plus — in Work and Codex

You're right that your Plus plan does **not** give you the GPT-6 Pro/Astra option in ordinary Chat.

But current OpenAI documentation says:

> **Plus includes GPT-6 Astra in ChatGPT Work and Codex.**

GPT-6 Pro/Astra **in Chat** is for Pro $100/$200, Business and Enterprise. citeturn0search0turn0search1

So your situation is:

| Surface | Your Plus plan |
|---|---|
| Normal Chat | GPT-6 Sol |
| GPT-6 Pro/Astra in normal Chat | ❌ |
| **Astra in Work** | **✅ limited usage** |
| **Astra in Codex** | **✅ limited usage** |
| Extra High | ❌ |
| Astra Ultrafast | ❌ |

And OpenAI explicitly says Plus gets limited Astra usage in Work/Codex, with credits available afterward. citeturn0search1turn0search4

**That means I would not recommend upgrading to Pro merely to experiment with Astra.**

Use the Astra you already have first.

---

# 5. Should we start using Codex?

### Yes — but not replace Claude with it.

For what you're doing now, I think we're actually **underusing Codex**.

urlOpenAI — Using Codex with your ChatGPT planturn2search3

Codex now has several things directly relevant to you: local repositories and terminals, Git worktrees for parallel tasks, cloud environments, remote access, scheduled tasks, Computer Use, usage information, and Astra. Codex Cloud jobs can continue even when your computer sleeps; local jobs naturally still depend on the host. citeturn2search3turn2search0

So I'd divide work like this:

```text
ChatGPT Chat
thinking / discussion / architecture / challenge

ChatGPT Work
research / long multi-step knowledge work / artifacts

Codex Local
repository + terminal + tests + applications

Codex Cloud
long coding job that shouldn't depend on laptop

Claude Code + Mods
Claude development + custom control-plane UI

Git
permanent shared truth
```

That is stronger than trying to make one AI do everything.

---

# 6. And OpenAI actually has something very close to the direction you're describing

**Dots.**

Current OpenAI documentation says a dot gets its **own cloud computer**. More interestingly, local-computer access can be enabled through ChatGPT Desktop. Once permitted, the dot can access files/work on that machine and can create **Work or Codex tasks**, use local skills and use the local browser. citeturn2search7

That architecture is important for our thinking:

```text
                  Senthil
                     │
                     ▼
                    DOT
              persistent agent
                     │
          ┌──────────┼──────────┐
          ▼          ▼          ▼
        Work       Codex      Apps
          │          │
          │      ┌───┴────┐
          │      ▼        ▼
          │    Cloud     Local
          │               │
          └───────────────┤
                          ▼
                         Git
```

Conceptually, **Dot is closer to the high-level orchestrator you're imagining**, while Claude Mods are closer to an extremely programmable Claude-Code-level control plane.

They aren't direct competitors at exactly the same layer.

---

# 7. Can Claude Mod orchestrate ChatGPT, Perplexity, Sarvam, etc.?

**Technically it could call external systems if we build adapters. But I would not make Claude Mod our global orchestrator.**

A Mod can run code and interact with permitted external services. So we could theoretically have:

```text
Claude Mod
   ├── Anthropic API
   ├── OpenAI API
   ├── Sarvam API
   └── other services
```

But your specific question is crucial:

> Can the Mod put something into *this ChatGPT page*?

**Not generically.**

Claude doesn't receive magical permission to write into arbitrary ChatGPT conversations merely because a Mod exists.

Similarly, **I cannot arbitrarily inject a prompt into another one of your existing ChatGPT chats from this normal chat.**

That is why Git has unexpectedly become so valuable in what we've built.

Instead of:

```text
Claude page ─────► ChatGPT page
```

we make:

```text
                 GLOBAL CONTROL PLANE
                         │
                 Git + Queue + State
                         │
       ┌─────────────────┼────────────────┐
       ▼                 ▼                ▼
 Claude worker      OpenAI worker     Sarvam worker
       │                 │                │
       └─────────────────┼────────────────┘
                         ▼
                       Git
```

Each vendor becomes a **worker**.

That is much safer than making Claude the king of everything.

---

# 8. This is where I agree strongly with your "remove me" observation

Not remove you from **decisions**.

Remove you from **mechanical coordination**.

Previously:

```text
AI finishes
   ↓
Senthil downloads
   ↓
Senthil moves file
   ↓
Senthil uploads
   ↓
Senthil tells another AI
   ↓
Senthil checks Git
   ↓
Senthil asks "did you Git Turn?"
   ↓
Senthil finds forgotten task
```

That is exactly the wrong place to spend your attention.

The target should become:

```text
                    SENTHIL
                direction / judgment
                       │
                       ▼
                  ORCHESTRATOR
                       │
             ┌─────────┼─────────┐
             ▼         ▼         ▼
          Claude    ChatGPT    others
             │         │
             └────┬────┘
                  ▼
              validation
                  ▼
                 Git
                  ▼
              dashboard
                  │
                  ▼
Senthil sees only:
 decisions / exceptions / cost / risk / results
```

Then you spend more time thinking about **what should be built and why**, rather than moving ZIP files around.

That's the correct direction.

---

# 9. I also found your product-verification repo

You told me **not to perform that verification here**, so I haven't.

The existing repository is:

**`vsenthil7/project-verification-workbench`**

Its stated purpose is exactly what you remembered: verify rebuilt projects, whether they run, tests/gaps, distance to closure, and recommended work order. It is private and already follows Git Turn Protocol v1.2. Its current state contains real verification work on the first three projects, UraiFlow, Tenant pilot and the 12 MoPr items. fileciteturn40file0L2-L2

Its existing handover also already tells the next page to continue MoPr verification and build workbook v02. fileciteturn42file0L2-L2

So **do not create another verification repository. Use this one.**

Here is the prompt I want you to give that separate Claude page:

:::writing{variant="document" id="58321" title="Current Project Portfolio Reconciliation Prompt"}
Continue `vsenthil7/project-verification-workbench` under its pinned Git Turn Protocol v1.2.

First pull/read current `main` and bootstrap from `AGENTS.md`, the protocol pin, `context/current-state.md`, the latest handover, and the manifest. Do not begin from assumptions in an older workbook.

Important new context: Senthil reports that during 12–13 October 2026 Claude completed a major Git consolidation/rebuild of his projects. He reports that his GitHub estate is now approximately 93 repositories, intended to be private, and that the projects/products previously discussed have now been represented in Git.

Your job is to independently verify the CURRENT Git reality against the existing project-verification evidence.

Phase A — Inventory reconciliation

Enumerate the currently accessible repositories owned by `vsenthil7` and identify repositories belonging to Senthil's product/project portfolio.

Compare the current Git inventory against:
- the existing project-verification inventory;
- the previous 12-product / MoPr records;
- earlier product lists;
- any new Git-native source-of-truth, handover, migration, rebuild, curation or consolidation evidence created during 12–13 October.

Classify every candidate as:
- VERIFIED CURRENT PRODUCT
- PROBABLE PRODUCT
- DUPLICATE / HISTORICAL / ARCHIVE
- SUPPORT / INFRASTRUCTURE REPO
- MISSING
- UNKNOWN

Do not delete, rename, archive, overwrite or change visibility of anything.

Phase B — Lineage and source of truth

For every confirmed product identify, where evidence permits:
- canonical repository;
- product name;
- purpose;
- latest meaningful commit;
- latest build/package/version lineage;
- tests/gates already proven;
- unresolved defects/gaps;
- whether previous verification evidence remains valid after the Git consolidation;
- duplicate or predecessor repositories;
- confidence and evidence source.

Do not silently resolve contradictory evidence. Preserve competing possibilities and mark UNKNOWN where evidence is insufficient.

Phase C — Re-verification strategy

Determine the minimum re-verification required after the consolidation.

Do NOT rerun expensive test suites simply to reproduce already-valid evidence unless the underlying product content materially changed.

Prioritize:
1. products changed after previous verification;
2. products never verified;
3. ambiguous canonical repositories;
4. products with known failing gates;
5. stale or contradictory evidence.

Explicitly identify and reconcile the “12 projects/products” Senthil referred to with the current repository inventory.

Phase D — Deliverables

Update this repository's evidence-backed:
- product inventory;
- current state;
- verification status/report;
- open questions;
- recommended execution order;
- latest handover / next-page prompt.

Preserve raw source evidence.

Follow Git Turn Protocol v1.2 for every material turn and land each turn on `main` in the same turn.

Do not perform Claude-memory or ChatGPT-memory export/reconstruction work in this task. That is a separate workstream.

At the end, tell Senthil:
1. what Git currently proves exists;
2. which products are canonical;
3. what changed since the previous verification;
4. what remains uncertain;
5. exactly what should be verified next and why.
:::

That is ready for the other page.

---

## 10. About exporting my ChatGPT context/memory like Claude

**Yes, this is worth doing, but separately.**

I don't want us to simply copy Claude's structure blindly.

The better goal is a **vendor-neutral context ledger**:

```text
RAW EXPORTS
    │
    ├── Claude
    ├── ChatGPT
    ├── Perplexity
    └── future AI
          │
          ▼
     NORMALIZATION
          │
     ┌────┼─────┐
     ▼    ▼     ▼
 facts events decisions
     │    │     │
     └────┼─────┘
          ▼
 provenance + confidence
          ▼
 contradictions
          ▼
 chronology
          ▼
 Git knowledge/context layer
```

Claude can absolutely do the heavy ZIP extraction if it is good at that bulk task. I can then independently review the **schema, semantic loss, contradictions and missing context**.

That's much better than keeping "Claude memory" and "ChatGPT memory" as separate permanent silos.

---

# The architecture is becoming clearer

I would now describe what we're building as:

```text
                         SENTHIL
                            │
                   goals / decisions
                            │
                            ▼
              GLOBAL AI CONTROL PLANE
             Git + Queue + State + Events
                            │
       ┌────────────────────┼───────────────────┐
       ▼                    ▼                   ▼
 Claude ecosystem     OpenAI ecosystem     Other models
       │                    │                   │
 Mods / Code          Dot / Work / Codex   API / agents
       │                    │                   │
       └────────────────────┼───────────────────┘
                            ▼
                    deterministic QA
                            │
                            ▼
                        Git-TURN
                            │
                            ▼
                         Git truth
                            │
                            ▼
                        Dashboard
```

**Claude Mod should be a powerful Claude-side control panel. It should not become our universal database or universal orchestrator.**

Git + a vendor-neutral job/state layer should remain above the vendors.

That way tomorrow, if Claude has a five-hour limit, **Codex can continue**. If Codex hits a limit, another worker can continue. If you change vendors entirely, the history, state, evidence and unfinished jobs remain yours.

### Git Evidence

- **Repo:** `vsenthil7/ai-tool-support-kb` · `main`
- **Turn:** T039 · **Read at:** `93980c6f`
- **Commit:** `428f54b`
- **Verified:** remote `main` = `428f54b070e628118fcbd652e5427ac6eeec05e5` fileciteturn73file0L2-L2
- **Research:** fresh official Anthropic + OpenAI documentation; GitHub inspection of `project-verification-workbench`
- **Important finding:** your Plus plan **already includes limited Astra access in Work and Codex**; it is Astra-in-normal-Chat/GPT-6 Pro that you don't have. citeturn0search0turn0search1
- **Protocol gap:** T039 turn record and usage landed in the single commit, but the timeline update was blocked during the Git write. I have **not hidden that gap**; it needs additive repair in the next `_kb` turn rather than rewriting this commit.

Yes — **you were referring to Claude Mods**, and my previous answer misinterpreted “MOD” as “mode/models.” After searching the current material, I found the feature you meant.

More importantly, your memory of what you saw is substantially right: **Mods can create live UI inside Claude Code, observe agents/jobs, intercept events, coordinate workflows, and community Mods already implement cross-session communication and operational dashboards.** Anthropic only announced Mods on **October 1, 2026**, so this is genuinely very recent. citeturn2view0

## What exactly is a Claude Mod?

A Claude Mod is **not another Claude model** and not simply a Skill.

Anthropic describes Mods as small TypeScript functions that can change how Claude Code itself behaves. A Mod can intercept Claude Code events before/after/instead of the normal behavior. It can rewrite prompts, block/retry tool calls, approve/deny permissions, redact tool output, create UI, add buttons and inputs, and even replace built-in Claude Code functionality. Anthropic says you can even ask Claude Code to **write a Mod for Claude Code**, install it, and hot-reload it. citeturn2view0

So conceptually:

```text
Normal plugin
    ↓
adds capabilities

Skill
    ↓
teaches Claude how to perform something

Hook
    ↓
runs when an event occurs

MOD
    ↓
can intercept + modify + replace + visualize
Claude Code's own behaviour
```

That last capability is what makes this especially interesting for us.

---

# Your "dashboard" observation was correct

This is where I initially missed your point.

Mods can draw **native panes beside the Claude transcript**, put information above the prompt, display buttons/status, react to events, maintain state, inspect session information, and update the UI while Claude is working. Anthropic specifically gives CI/CD status shown in a pane beside the conversation as an example. citeturn2view0

And community developers have already gone much further.

For example, **Claude Flightdeck** is a Mod showing a live agent dashboard with model/effort, context consumption, cost, permission decisions, subagents, timelines and a turn receipt. citeturn0search4turn0search15

Another Mod, **Agent Flow**, shows a live tree of subagents and teammates — what each is doing, elapsed time, current tool call, approvals, calls and token information. citeturn0search2turn0search8

A **session-dashboard** Mod shows cache state, tool calls/errors, background commands, approved plans, task lists, subagents/swarm agents and token consumption. citeturn4search13

So your idea:

> "I have multiple jobs/pages running. I want one dashboard over them."

is **no longer something we necessarily have to build entirely outside Claude Code.**

That's the big discovery.

---

# And you remembered the "pages talking to each other" part too

This is where the research became particularly interesting.

There are already Mods exploring exactly that.

**Crosstalk** opens a pane containing conversations between the current Claude Code session and other Claude Code sessions and lets one session reply to another. citeturn4search1

**Session Bridge** goes even further: it is described as allowing Claude Code sessions to talk to other sessions, including **meetings between two sessions**. citeturn4search6

**Session Ref** lets a prompt reference an earlier session ID and injects a digest containing prompts, files, commits and the last response. citeturn4search8

**Session Watch** can display the other Claude sessions running on the machine alongside model, context, token, cost and Git information. citeturn4search9

There is also an official Anthropic feature called **Agent View**. It gives one view of Claude Code sessions, shows which ones are working/waiting/completed, lets you peek at them and reply without fully switching sessions, and supports background jobs. citeturn0search0

So there are actually **three layers** here:

| Layer | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Agent View** | Official multi-session manager |
| **Claude Mods** | Programmable Claude Code UI/event/control system |
| **Community Mods** | Dashboards, cross-session messaging, observability, automation, etc. |

That combination is much closer to what you were describing.

---

# But there is another "Dashboard" — don't mix these two

Anthropic separately launched **Claude Dashboards on October 8**, only five days ago.

This is a different product.

Claude Dashboards connects to data systems such as BigQuery, Databricks, Snowflake, Redshift or Salesforce, builds a live dashboard from a plain-English question, and keeps it refreshed as the source data changes. Every chart can expose the query behind it. citeturn3view0

So:

```text
CLAUDE MOD DASHBOARD
────────────────────
"What are my AI agents doing?"

sessions
jobs
agents
tokens
cost
permissions
Git
errors
queue
context
progress


CLAUDE DASHBOARDS
────────────────────
"What is my business/data doing?"

BigQuery
Snowflake
Salesforce
Databricks
KPIs
charts
metrics
analytics
```

They are separate — but we could eventually connect them.

That becomes extremely interesting.

---

# Now relate this directly to what **we** have been building

Previously our thinking was approximately:

```text
Claude pages
ChatGPT pages
Perplexity
Sarvam
      ↓
     Git
      ↓
Build our own dashboard
      ↓
Monitor everything
```

I would **not throw that architecture away**.

But I would change it.

### New architecture

```text
                  SENTHIL
                     │
                     ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────┐
        │  SENTHIL CONTROL PLANE  │
        │      Claude MOD         │
        └─────────────────────────┘
                     │
       ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
       ▼             ▼             ▼
    Sessions       Agents        Jobs
       │             │             │
       └─────────────┼─────────────┘
                     ▼
               Git-TURN layer
                     │
       ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
       ▼             ▼             ▼
    Evidence       State        History
       │             │             │
       └─────────────┼─────────────┘
                     ▼
                 Git repos
```

**Mod = live control plane.**

**Git = durable truth.**

That's a much stronger combination than choosing one or the other.

---

# What I think we should eventually build

I'd call it something temporarily like:

**`senthil-control-plane`**

Not necessarily the final name.

It could have perhaps **8 panels**.

**Sessions / Jobs** would show every active Claude job, status, start time, last activity, current task, blocked/waiting/running/done.

**Git-TURN** would show something like:

```text
Session A    T038   ✓ committed
Session B    T127   ⚠ response not committed
Session C    T044   ✓ verified
Session D    -----  🔴 Git Turn missing
```

That alone would solve one of your recurring frustrations.

**Usage** could show:

```text
Claude plan
Session usage
Weekly usage
Tokens
Context %
Compactions
Estimated API equivalent
```

We have already been building some of this separately in `_kb`.

**Agents** could visualize:

```text
Main Claude
 ├── Researcher        RUNNING
 ├── Transcript Agent  DONE
 ├── Reviewer          WAITING
 └── Git Agent         BLOCKED
```

Very similar to Flightdeck/Agent Flow.

**Evidence** could expose:

```text
RAW
DERIVED
INFERENCE
UNKNOWN
UNVERIFIED
```

which matches our evidence philosophy.

**Queue** could implement your earlier FIFO idea:

```text
#183  Running
#184  Waiting
#185  Waiting
#186  Retry 1/3
#187  Paused
```

**Permissions** could show exactly what an agent wants to do before it does it.

And **Handover** could show:

```text
Current state
Last completed turn
Open questions
Pending tasks
Next-page prompt
Other active sessions
```

Now the system starts looking like an actual **AI operations console**.

---

# One particularly important possibility

You have repeatedly complained about this:

> **"Why did you forget the Git Turn?"**

Currently we're trying to solve that with **instructions**.

Mods give us the possibility of solving it at a **system level**.

Conceptually:

```text
Claude says:
"I'm finished."

       ↓

MOD intercepts completion

       ↓

Git-TURN exists?
Usage exists?
Timeline updated?
Secret scan passed?
Commit exists?
Remote verified?

       ↓

NO ──────→ Don't allow clean completion
             "Protocol incomplete"

YES ─────→ ✓ COMPLETE
```

That's fundamentally different from writing:

> "Claude, please remember Git Turn."

**The system itself can enforce it.**

That is probably the single biggest relevance of Mods to our current work.

---

# But I would NOT install 50 Mods now

Anthropic explicitly warns that Mods run with the **same machine access as Claude Code** and are **not sandboxed**. citeturn2view0

That's important.

A random Mod can potentially be much more consequential than a browser extension.

So our sequence should be:

**Research → inspect source → test isolated → read-only first → permit controlled actions → only then production use.**

Especially on the machine containing all your Git repositories.

---

# Your YouTube Short

I tried to access the Short you supplied, but the video itself wasn't retrievable through my web access.

So **yes, send me the screenshots**.

They are now much more useful because I know what I'm looking for. I can identify each item in the Short and classify it as:

**official Anthropic feature / built-in Mod / community Mod / separate Claude feature / creator's own custom Mod / speculation.**

Then we can make a table:

```text
Feature shown
      ↓
What it really is
      ↓
Official/community?
      ↓
What it can do
      ↓
Security level
      ↓
Useful for us?
      ↓
Already have equivalent?
      ↓
Build / install / ignore
```

## And there is a correction to my previous turn

T037 should **not be deleted** because our Git protocol is additive.

I have recorded this turn as **T038**, explicitly correcting T037:

> **Claude MOD = Claude Mods**, not merely Claude modes/models.

That correction is now preserved in `_kb`.

Yes. I’m reading **“Claude mod” as “Claude modes/features”**, particularly Claude Code and its newer agentic capabilities.

I also followed your `_kb` instruction. The repository is **`vsenthil7/ai-tool-support-kb`**, and its active standard is **Git Turn Protocol v1.2**. The protocol requires one material turn → one Git record, usage tracking, timeline update, and remote verification. fileciteturn4file0L2-L2 This turn is now **T037** and is committed on `main` as `706e351`. fileciteturn18file0L2-L2

# What Claude's features actually mean for us

The useful way to understand Claude is **not as one AI chat window**. It is increasingly a stack:

**Model → effort/reasoning → planning → Skills → subagents → tools/MCP → automation → Git → verification**

That is extremely relevant to what we have been building.

## 1. Model + effort = choose how much intelligence to spend

Anthropic now supports different Claude models and increasingly explicit control over how much effort Claude puts into a task. Their newer Opus releases also support faster execution options and larger agentic workflows. citeturn0search0turn0search5

For us, don't use maximum intelligence for everything.

| Our work | Suggested approach |
|---|---|
| Rename/format/extract data | Fast/cheap |
| Transcript classification | Fast/cheap |
| KB entry generation | Normal |
| Research | Normal/high |
| Architecture | High |
| Difficult debugging | High |
| Postmortem | High |
| Protocol changes | High |
| Final independent review | High/separate agent |

### Benefit

This addresses one of the problems we've already discussed: **why spend expensive reasoning tokens on mechanical work?**

Our future router should decide:

> **Task → complexity → model → effort → tools → reviewer**

rather than sending everything to the most expensive Claude.

---

# 2. Skills — this may be one of the most valuable Claude features for us

Anthropic's **Skills** are reusable folders containing instructions, scripts and resources. Claude loads a Skill when the current task requires it rather than stuffing all of those instructions into every prompt. Skills can also be combined and reused across Claude apps, Claude Code and the API. citeturn0search1

This maps almost perfectly to what you've been trying to create.

Instead of repeatedly telling Claude:

> Don't forget Git Turn.  
> Preserve raw evidence.  
> Don't overwrite.  
> Update timeline.  
> Check usage.  
> Do postmortem.  
> Verify sources...

we should eventually package these behaviours.

For example:

```text
skills/
    git-turn/
    transcript-ingest/
    evidence-preservation/
    source-verification/
    postmortem/
    kb-builder/
    kb-reviewer/
    usage-recorder/
    next-page-handover/
```

Then you say:

> Analyse this call and postmortem it.

Claude can invoke the relevant Skills rather than requiring you to repeat 30 instructions.

### Benefit for you

This attacks something that has been irritating you repeatedly:

**"Why do I have to remind the AI again about Git?"**

The long-term answer shouldn't be **better reminders from you**.

It should be:

> **Encode the behaviour once.**

---

# 3. Subagents — Claude can create specialist workers

Anthropic's current guidance explicitly discusses Claude orchestrating **subagents**. It also warns that agents shouldn't be spawned unnecessarily; simple tasks are often better done directly. citeturn1search0

We already have the beginning of this idea in `_kb`: T023 created **KB Builder + KB Reviewer** agents.

Our mature version could look like:

```text
                    ORCHESTRATOR
                         |
        +----------------+----------------+
        |                |                |
   Researcher         Builder         Evidence Agent
        |                |                |
        +----------------+----------------+
                         |
                      Reviewer
                         |
                    Git-TURN QA
```

For your call/transcript work, for example:

**Researcher**
→ establishes external facts.

**Transcript/Evidence agent**
→ preserves what was actually said.

**Analyst**
→ interprets it.

**Skeptic**
→ searches for alternative explanations.

**Reviewer**
→ asks whether the conclusions are actually supported.

**Git agent**
→ makes sure the entire exercise survives the chat page.

### Benefit

This is much stronger than asking the **same model to create something and then congratulate itself for creating it correctly**.

---

# 4. MCP / connectors — connect Claude to the actual world

MCP/connectors allow Claude to interact with external systems rather than having you manually copy information into prompts.

Potential architecture for us:

```text
Claude
   |
   +--- GitHub
   +--- Google Drive
   +--- Browser
   +--- Database
   +--- Files
   +--- APIs
   +--- Internal tools
```

Anthropic is continuing to expand connector-based workflows across its products. citeturn0search3

But I would **not** connect everything with write access.

Our rule should be:

```text
READ
  ↓
ANALYSE
  ↓
PROPOSE
  ↓
VERIFY
  ↓
WRITE
```

And start with **least privilege**.

### Benefit

You stop being the human API:

> Download this → upload here → copy that → paste there → ask Claude → copy result → upload elsewhere.

That manual glue can gradually disappear.

---

# 5. Hooks/scripts — extremely important for your Git problem

There are things we should **not trust an LLM to remember**.

Example:

```text
Claude finishes work
       ↓
secret scan
       ↓
protocol validator
       ↓
tests
       ↓
Git-TURN exists?
       ↓
usage exists?
       ↓
timeline updated?
       ↓
commit
       ↓
remote verification
```

Your `_kb` protocol already requires secret checking, one commit per turn, timeline tracking and remote verification. fileciteturn5file0L2-L2

The important architectural principle is:

> **LLM handles judgment. Code enforces invariants.**

So instead of hoping Claude remembers Git-TURN every time, a validator should eventually reject completion when Git-TURN is absent.

That is much stronger.

---

# 6. Long-running / dynamic workflows

This is another major development.

Anthropic's guidance now explicitly discusses **long-horizon work across context windows**, persistent progress/state, tests, setup scripts and using Git as state tracking. citeturn1search0

Opus 4.8 also introduced **dynamic workflows** in Claude Code aimed at much larger tasks. citeturn0search0

This fits your earlier requirement:

> Don't send 10,000 things at once.

Correct.

Our pattern should be:

```text
TASK QUEUE
   ↓
Pick batch
   ↓
Research
   ↓
Execute
   ↓
Verify
   ↓
Commit
   ↓
Record outcome
   ↓
Next batch
```

If the context dies after batch 37, the next agent reads Git and starts at **38**.

It doesn't need to "remember."

---

# 7. Git becomes the common memory between ALL AIs

This is perhaps the most important connection.

Anthropic itself recommends Git as a useful mechanism for state tracking during long-running agentic work. citeturn1search0

That's exactly where your idea becomes larger than Claude.

We shouldn't design:

```text
Senthil
   ↓
Claude
```

We should design:

```text
                Git
                 |
      +----------+----------+
      |          |          |
   Claude     ChatGPT   Perplexity
      |          |          |
      +----------+----------+
                 |
             Evidence
                 |
             Decisions
                 |
              State
```

Then Claude can disappear tomorrow.

ChatGPT can disappear.

Perplexity can disappear.

A new model can arrive.

The **project survives**.

---

# 8. Where Skills + subagents + Git become powerful together

Imagine you give one command:

> **Postmortem today's Subha/IPBS calls.**

The system could eventually perform:

```text
1. Git-TURN Skill starts
2. Evidence Skill locates source material
3. Transcript agent preserves raw transcript
4. Research agent checks external claims
5. Analyst extracts events
6. Skeptic generates competing hypotheses
7. Timeline agent reconstructs chronology
8. Reviewer challenges unsupported conclusions
9. Action agent extracts next steps
10. Git validator checks everything
11. Commit
12. Usage/cost recorded
13. Dashboard updated
```

You receive the result.

That is much closer to the system you've actually been describing over the last several days.

---

# 9. What I would build first

I **wouldn't chase every new Claude feature**.

Our order should be:

**Phase 1 — Git backbone**

Keep Git Turn v1.2 as the source-of-truth mechanism.

**Phase 2 — five core Skills**

```text
git-turn
evidence-ingest
research-verification
builder
reviewer
```

**Phase 3 — deterministic validation**

Make it mechanically difficult for Claude/ChatGPT to finish without the required Git artefacts.

**Phase 4 — intelligent routing**

```text
Task
 ↓
Simple? ──→ Direct/cheap
 ↓ no
Parallel? ─→ Subagents
 ↓
High consequence? ─→ High effort + reviewer
```

**Phase 5 — MCP/connectors**

Only add integrations that remove actual manual work.

**Phase 6 — measurement**

Track:

```text
cost
tokens
latency
retries
agent count
failures
review findings
human corrections
task success
```

Then we can answer scientifically:

> Did multi-agent Claude actually improve the outcome?

rather than assuming that more agents = better.

---

# The bigger architecture I recommend for us

```text
                     SENTHIL
                        |
                        v
                  ORCHESTRATOR
                        |
              +---------+---------+
              |                   |
          TASK ROUTER         RISK ROUTER
              |                   |
       model / effort       permissions
              |
      +-------+-------+
      |       |       |
   Skills  Agents   MCP/Tools
      |       |       |
      +-------+-------+
              |
        WORK / RESEARCH
              |
        DETERMINISTIC QA
              |
          REVIEW AGENT
              |
        GIT-TURN PROTOCOL
              |
             GIT
              |
      +-------+-------+
      |               |
   Dashboard        RAG/Search
```

That is **vendor-neutral**.

Claude can be the best worker for some steps. ChatGPT can handle others. Perplexity can research. Sarvam can handle Indian-language transcription. Future models can enter without redesigning the whole system.

## Most important conclusion

**Skills + subagents are very valuable for us.**

But **Git + deterministic validation are more important.**

Because Skills make Claude smarter at our workflow.

Subagents make Claude more scalable.

MCP gives Claude reach.

High-effort reasoning gives Claude intelligence.

But **Git makes the entire system recoverable, inspectable and transferable between AIs.**

So I would build:

> **Git as memory → Skills as reusable knowledge → Agents as workers → MCP as hands → models as replaceable brains → deterministic validation as safety/control.**

That is much closer to the AI operating system you have been gradually designing than simply "using Claude better."
